purpose: Test valve-receiver overload and obtain a non-clipping control without changing the probe-.22 HTV145 assignment protocol.

unchanged_from_prior_trial: assignment bytes apart from clock and trailer

normalized_phy_comparison.method: median instantaneous frequency from the interior half of each recovered alternating wake symbol; reply center is normalized to the valve request from the same session

superseded_fft_estimate.reason: An unconstrained FFT selected data-dependent sidebands rather than equally weighting the two alternating FSK tones. These values must not be used for transmitter calibration.

power_comparison.measurement_note: Active samples use magnitude greater than 10 ADC units over the assignment burst. The reduced-power burst had no exact 0/255 I/Q samples.

interpretation: The 0 dBm override was applied: active captured magnitude fell by 12.69 dB and ADC-rail clipping fell from 45.9 percent to zero.
The valve still rejected the same counter-0 selector-6 assignment before emitting an addressed stage-1 request, so transmit-power overload is not the missing enrollment prerequisite.

Balanced-wake analysis invalidates the earlier FFT carrier/deviation conclusion: stock uses the approximately 41.260 kHz CC1101 0x45 profile, while local probe .22 used the approximately 34.912 kHz 0x43 profile.

After normalizing each assignment against the valve request oscillator from the same session, local probe .22 was 35.370 kHz below stock. Absolute SDR center comparisons across sessions had hidden this error.

Clipping made amplitude and unconstrained spectral-peak selection unreliable in the prior local capture, but it did not invalidate the exact decoded frame, protocol ordering, or bounded request/reply timing.

Probe .23 must change only the independently disproven initial carrier calibration and deviation register. Payload, endpoints, selector, wake, timing, power, polarity, and one-shot state behavior remain frozen.
